counting_unit: Two existing logical inventory groups reassessed against a higher-resolution edition. Neither is a new distinct target.

records.supported_name_scope: The complete selected New South Wales path runs southeast from a northwestern headwater, south through the upper and middle corridor, then southeast to a southern bend before turning east and northeast to the coast south of Lismore. Its regional geography remains compatible with the Richmond River candidate. In the newly acquired high-resolution chapter, neighbouring Clarence, Boyd, Macleay and Manning line names are legible, but no direct Richmond river-line label is established in the inspected Figures 4.1, 4.22–4.27, 4.34, 4.35 or 4.45. Figure 4.22 supplies a Richmond River catchment callout, and Table 4.4 a Richmond River entry in the River basin column for Lismore. Rocky Creek in Figure 4.35 labels an urban-storage symbol, not the complete selected river. The prior ambiguity about potentially blurred Richmond lettering is replaced for these checked views by a bounded no-direct-label finding. Representative identity and whole-group naming remain on hold after complete-path reassessment. Headwater or feeder names, exact river/storage relationships, name transitions and the coastal ending remain unassigned at reach level.
limits: The direct-name gap persists in the inspected high-resolution New South Wales maps despite clearly readable neighbouring river names. This is a bounded result for the cited figures, not a claim that no direct Richmond or Hastings evidence exists elsewhere.

Grey catchment callouts and entries in the River basin column do not establish which river name applies to the complete selected modeled path. A modeled MAIN_RIV/mainstem role does not establish one real-world name for every part.
Flow values, salinity and variability symbols, flood-class dots, storage triangles and wetland callouts do not supply named-station identities or exact selected river-reach names.
The high-resolution chapter and earlier low-resolution full report are editions of one publication and one source group. Their hydrographic dataset independence has not been verified.
Original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality, exact feeder and reach-name transitions, selected-path storage crossings, tidal boundaries and the surveyed mouth are not established.

The rendered sea ending differs from retained baseline source-endpoint metadata. Those metadata are not independently verified original HydroRIVERS coordinates; no river name is extended over that difference.

prior_public_assessment.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path descends south from its northwestern headwater and then follows an eastward corridor to the Port Macquarie coast. It corresponds geographically to mapped channels within the Hastings River catchment context. Hastings River is a geographic candidate only: Figure 4.22 provides a catchment leader and Table 4.4 a River basin entry, but no direct Hastings river-line label or named Hastings station was established in the inspected maps. This does not support representative river identity or name coverage over the complete selected group. The modeled mainstem role does not name the headwater or feeder course, storage interfaces or coastal ending. The whole-group naming scope remains on hold.
